content: It currently looks like there are a few issues about unindexed repos outstanding. (Indeed, it looks to me like they meet the criteria and aren't indexed, most of the issues are over a week old, so it's not a issue resolved by waiting for another indexing pass). @Mac Malone are you sure you reenabled the workflow mentioned in this thread (#general > ✔ Lean reservoir no updated )?

It's enabled. We have reached a scale factor where it has become increasingly uncommon for packages to be caught in the general search. I am able to manual index packages, but I have been otherwise occupied. The FRO is also working on new infrastructure that will be useful to Reservoir and hopefully scale better. We knew there were limitations to the current approach, but it was sufficient for the initial push when the ecosystem was small.

@Mac Malone one thing that would be great for reservoir is just a register feature embedded with lake tooling. This way users could self register their project instead of reservoir needing to rely on github search feature.
A nice value of self registration feature would be to add categories to projects. categories would allow to distinguish projects like :

  • Maths library
  • Physics library
  • Computer science library
  • Software library
  • Software executable

This would allow better discoverability.

@Alfredo Moreira-Rosa Lake/Reservoir does have a keywords field for tagging projects by topic. The math Lake templates tag their projects math. These keywords appear on the package on Reservoir and can be used to narrow package search, e.g., https://reservoir.lean-lang.org/packages?keyword=math. Some bigger projects, e.g., Mathlib, were created long before this metadata was added and have not adopted it yet. I imagine there could be a push to tag such projects if users found that useful.

I didn't know! nice.
Yes i think a push to tag or any self service registration would be great. But i guess this demands some infra and work. i would be happy to help if you want to
I would also be happy to help if additional hands would be helpful.
